OBSERVATIONS AND CORRECTIVE ACTIONS
1 - Observation: Valid food managers certification is required and was not available upon request at the point of inspection. Facility or PIC must ensure at least one individual within the facility must acquire a valid food managers certification within 60 days of their employment. Also, individuals designated to obtain the food handlers certification are required to obtain the certification within 30 days of their employment. Both certifications must be made available upon request at the time of inspection.  
Code Section: 113947.1 
Correct By: 11/14/2026
6 - Observation: Observed the bar handwashing sink without paper towels readily available within a dispenser. Provide hot and cold running water under pressure, single use soap and paper towels in dispensers. 
Code Section: 113953.2 
Correct By: 10/21/2026
23 - Observation: Observed a multitude of drain flies within the bar area, primarily within the floor sink. Once indicated to the PIC, PIC was instructed to contact a pest control provider to adequately remove the flies from within the facility. Also, PIC/facility must thoroughly clean and sanitize all contaminated areas. Maintain a relationship with pest operator as a means of eradicating and preventing pest infestations. 
Code Section: 114259.1 
Correct By: 10/14/2026
33 - Observation: Observed dust accumulation on the blower fan covers inside the walk-in refrigeration unit. Maintain an environment free of dust and debris. Clean nonfood-contact surface and maintain in sanitary condition. 
Code Section: 114115(c) 
Correct By: 10/21/2026
Corrective Action: Clean nonfood-contact surface and maintain in sanitary condition. 
34 - Observation: Observed the temperature gauges associated with the bar warewashing machine was not functioning. PIC/Facility must contact a service provider to ensure the machine can accurately measure water temperature. 
Code Section: 114099.5 
Correct By: 10/28/2026
39 - Observation: At time of inspection, no appropriate temperature measuring device were available in multiple refrigeration units for adequate food temperature monitoring. Provide a thermometer accurate to +/- 2F in each refrigeration unit; maintain an approved metal probe thermometer onsite suitable for measuring food temperatures. 
Code Section: 114157 
Correct By: 10/21/2026
Corrective Action: Provide a thermometer accurate to +/- 2°F in each refrigeration unit; maintain an approved metal probe thermometer onsite suitable for measuring food temperatures. 
39 - Observation: At time of inspection, no appropriate temperature measuring device was available for adequate internal food temperature monitoring. Provide a thermometer accurate to +/- 2F in each refrigeration unit; maintain an approved metal probe thermometer onsite suitable for measuring food temperatures. 
Code Section: 114159 
Correct By: 10/21/2026
Corrective Action: Provide a thermometer accurate to +/- 2°F in each refrigeration unit; maintain an approved metal probe thermometer onsite suitable for measuring food temperatures. 
40 - Observation: Observed the sanitizing solution bucket in the food preparation. Ensure any/all sanitizing buckets are properly prepared with an approved sanitizer at the required concentration and is maintained with the appropriate wiping cloth when in use. Verify sanitizer concentration using an appropriate test strip and maintain the solution at the required chemical concentration. 
Code Section: 114185.1 
Correct By: 10/21/2026
44 - Observation: Observed the entrance/exiting door with visible light emitting from the bottom and sides of the door. Exiting door needs to remain closed or install a viable means to prevent the potential entering of vermin/insects from harboring within the facility. PIC was instructed to fix the doors or alternative methods to ensure employee kitchen area is fully enclosed. Maintain the facility to prevent the entrance and/or harborage of animals, birds, and vermin. 
Code Section: 114259 
Correct By: 10/21/2026
45 - Observation: Observed an accumulation of food debris within the floor sink within the bar area of the facility. PIC was instructed to deep clean the floor sink and maintain facility in a condition that could not be characterized as unsanitary. Maintain and clean floors, walls and ceilings in food preparation, food storage, utensil wash, restroom, and food service area(s). 
Code Section: 114268.1 
Correct By: 10/21/2026
45 - Observation: Observed significant amount of molded food debris within the bar floor sink. PIC was instructed to deep clean the entire bar area and maintain facility in a condition that could not be characterized as unsanitary. Maintain and clean floors, walls and ceilings in food preparation, food storage, utensil wash, restroom, and food service area(s). 
Code Section: 114268.1 
Correct By: 10/21/2026

This is a NOTICE TO COMPLY. The required corrective action is described above. The governing laws are the California Health and Safety Code, Division 104, Part 7, RETAIL FOOD Chapters 1-13, otherwise known as the California Retail Food Code (Cal Code). The Napa County Department of Planning, Building, & Environmental Services may re-inspect the facility at any time to verify compliance with this Notice to Comply. Disputes to this inspection report must be made in writing within five (5) days of the signature date. Until such time as a decision is made regarding such a dispute, the contents of this report and the grade shall remain in effect. Please note that the Department uses a point system to grade facilities based on the number of points lost. 1-10 points deducted equals A; 11-20 points deducted equals B; 21-30 points equals C; greater than 30 points deducted equals a failed score (F), which necessitates immediate action and subjects the facility to additional inspections and/or legal actions to ensure the protection of the public health and safety. Facilities receiving two consecutive scores greater than 20 are subject to a re-inspection fee.

Major violations are those with a point value of 6 and minor violations are those with a point value of 2 or less. If, upon review by the Department, any errors are found that result in fewer points being deducted, the Department will make the correction and provide a copy of the corrected report to the facility owner/operator. The inspection report will be posted to the Internet no sooner than one County business day after the inspection is completed.
